data: © ESA / Roscosmos — ExoMars 2016 EDM. Premature parachute release caused free-fall impact at Meridiani Planum.

ExoMars 2016 Entry, Descent, Landing Demonstrator. A control software fault caused the inertial measurement unit to saturate, leading the lander to compute a negative altitude and triggering premature parachute and backshell jettison. The thrusters fired briefly as if already on the ground, then shut off. It free-fell ~3.7 km to the surface. The flight data informed the ExoMars 2028 EDL redesign.
Hard-won EDL diagnostic data — a partial demonstration that fed forward into the next ExoMars mission.

Schiaparelli — Europe's second Mars landing attempt — separated from ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter on October 16, 2016, then crashed into Meridiani Planum at ~540 km/h three days later. A software glitch caused the parachute and braking thrusters to disengage 50 seconds early, while the lander was still 3.7 km above the surface. The wreckage was spotted by MRO HiRISE within a week. Lessons learned shaped the ExoMars Rosalind Franklin rover, now slated for 2028 launch.
EDM — Entry, Descent, and Landing Demonstrator Module
Schiaparelli lander pre-launch — 577 kg, designed as a one-time technology demonstrator for the ExoMars rover EDL system.
Proton-M lifts off with the ExoMars 2016 stack — TGO + Schiaparelli, joint ESA-Roscosmos mission.
MRO HiRISE images the Schiaparelli impact site — main crater visible at top; parachute + backshell at lower right.
HiRISE detail of the Schiaparelli crash site — black streak left by hardware impact, surrounding ejecta blanket.
Computer-graphics reconstruction of the failure sequence — IMU saturation during parachute deployment caused premature lander release at 3.7 km altitude.
